To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new class of NIR-emitting 1D coordination polymer was synthesized and studied.
we have synthesized a new class of 1D polyplatinated cyanoximate complex that demonstrates NIR luminescence in a broad temperature range.

the 1D coordination polymer of the PtL2 type, with L = 2-cyanoxime ligand, was synthesized and studied for the first time; it was shown that this polymer is a "solid solution", containing mixed-valence species, and the emission of the polymer is caused by the presence of Pt(II)/IV centers; the emission is enhanced upon additional oxidation (by Br2 vapors) of Pt(II).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of a new class (to the best of our knowledge, the first) of NIR emissive platinum cyanoxime complexes, which could be used as NIR emitters and NIR imaging agents in the design of new NIR emitters.

the synthesis of new PtL2 complexes (L = ambidentate ligand) and the study of their structural, photophysical, and magnetic properties, which are important for the design of novel luminescent and magnetic materials.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found the first example of NIR emissive 1D polymer based on Pt(II) cyanoximate.
we have developed an approach to the synthesis of NIR emissive complexes with the use of PtL2 cyanoximate complexes, which are based on the Pt---Pt metallophilic interaction.
we were able to demonstrate the first example of NIR emission in the 1D coordination polymer of platinum cyanoximes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NIR emission in the 1000-1200 nm range can be achieved in a Pt(II) complex with an ambidentate mixed donor cyanoxime ligand.
the emission of the NIR region of the spectrum, which is of great importance for biomedical and optical imaging applications, is possible in the case of a 1D polyatomic Pt(II) cyanoximate.
the NIR emission of the Pt(II)/IV mixed-valence complex can be tuned over a wide range by changing the Pt---Pt bond length, which can be achieved by the choice of the appropriate ligands.
